headline: UPDATE TO totw-20261107-1900-03 (25 killed) -- IN-WINDOW
dek: Saudi-led strikes on homes in al-Shariya village, Sanaa province, killed 27 people (mostly women and children) and wounded 36; follow-up strikes targeted paramedics pulling survivors from rubble. UN: more than 1,600 killed and 300,000+ displaced since fighting resumed in Yemen.
sources: Ansar Allah-run Health Ministry (spokesman Anees Alasbahi) via AP and AFP; UN figures via AFP
fault_line: Who is killing Yemeni civilians -- Saudi air power or Ansar Allah forces staging from civilian areas -- and whether the revived Yemen war is a sideshow or the front line of the wider US-Iran war.

sections.what_happened: Saudi-led strikes on homes in al-Shariya village, Sanaa province, killed 27 people (mostly women and children) and wounded 36; follow-up strikes targeted paramedics pulling survivors from rubble. UN: more than 1,600 killed and 300,000+ displaced since fighting resumed in Yemen.
sections.what_verified: 2 distinct publisher families (AP, AFP) carry the ministry's updated toll; the figure itself remains single-source (the ministry). Saudi attribution of the strikes is unconfirmed by Riyadh.
sections.what_disputed: Saudi Arabia has not commented on the strikes or the toll; AP could not independently verify the claim; the toll has been revised four times in one day (11 -> 22 -> 25 -> 27), which is consistent with rubble recovery but also with single-source counting.
sections.why_matters: The toll keeps climbing while Riyadh stays silent: 27 dead near Sanaa, paramedics hit in follow-up strikes, and the UN counts 1,600+ dead since the truce collapsed -- the Yemen war is now the bloodiest front of the regional war.
sections.context: Background: UPDATE TO totw-20261107-1900-03 (25 killed) -- IN-WINDOW (Dawn liveblog 10:23pm PKT = 21:23 , AFP; Shafaq 2026-11-07T17:42:15Z = 21:42 ) -- Sanaa al-Shariya toll rises to 27 killed, 36 wounded; UN: 1,600+ killed and 300,000+ displaced since fighting resumed

totw_analysis: Our read: The toll keeps climbing while Riyadh stays silent: 27 dead near Sanaa, paramedics hit in follow-up strikes, and the UN counts 1,600+ dead since the truce collapsed -- the Yemen war is now the bloodiest front of the regional war. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Who is killing Yemeni civilians -- Saudi air power or Ansar Allah forces staging from civilian areas -- and whether the revived Yemen war is a sideshow or the front line of the wider US-Iran war.
